snapshot_note: Full source read includes committed ffaa486 and 65223e8 follow-ups that arrived during review. Findings bind this exact snapshot, not later fixes. No control-driver or fixture implementation clearance.

findings.title: Identity-query Popen holds the short failure latch
findings.reason: query.launch calls spawn under both state.lock and failure_lock. Production spawn is subprocess.Popen plus registration. If process creation blocks, _queue_stop cannot acquire failure_lock to retain an observer failure or wake signalling. The soft deadline explicitly wakes signalling first, but an earlier observer failure cannot rely on that later timer to satisfy prompt-stop and first-cause contracts.
findings.correction: Keep failure_lock memory-only. Reserve/check launch intent under short locking, release before Popen, then immediately register the returned child and check pending stop. If stop arrived during creation, retain the handle/history and trigger cleanup of that child without claiming zero instructions ran in the publication/creation gap. Preserve hard cutoff and one-query semantics.
findings.origin: Lead independently identified this same current-code blocker.

findings.title: Command child can arrive after the only escalation snapshots
findings.reason: command checks stopping while holding state.lock alone, then calls Popen. _queue_stop can queue failure and set stopping under failure_lock while that Popen is in flight. The one-shot signalling thread can take both TERM/KILL child snapshots before Popen returns and registration occurs. command does not recheck stop after registration and proceeds to persistence/identity observation. A late child can therefore survive the completed escalation until hard cutoff or later main cleanup.
findings.correction: Use the same explicit in-flight spawn/late-registration disposition for ordinary commands as for identity helpers. Once Popen returns, register first and, if stop is pending, immediately perform or schedule bound cleanup for that returned handle; do not repair this by holding failure_lock across Popen. Retain launch/registration/stopped-during-launch receipts.
findings.future_control: Inject a blocked command spawn, latch stop and allow escalation to complete before returning the fake child; its late registration must remain owned and receive cleanup without waiting until the hard deadline.

findings.title: Final CLEAR can omit a live registered child whose birth is unknown
findings.reason: register_child stores roots[pid]=None. discover_owned includes only matching PID/birth or discovered ancestry/group closure; a root with unknown birth is not included even if its PID is present. final_audit chooses CLEAR solely from returned rows and does not disposition remaining Popen handles/unknown registrations. On failed birth observation or incomplete cleanup this can overstate resource closure. An already latched failure prevents site PASS, but does not make the CLEAR process-audit claim sound.
findings.correction: Final audit must disposition every retained direct child/helper using its live/reaped handle state and recorded identity. A known-live handle means HELD; an unresolved registration means UNKNOWN_HELD. Never infer absence solely from a missing birth match, and never turn bare PID reuse into authority. Retain dispositions in the audit/history.
findings.future_control: Inject a live direct child with unknown birth, successful otherwise-valid global rows and no discoverable owned ancestry/group; final audit must not be CLEAR. Include unresolved handle and confirmed-reaped variants.

known_issue_dispositions.support: Successful snapshot lacking a later-published worker now remains pending without ACK; only declaration corruption and observed parent/group/birth mismatch fail immediately. Later successful observation is normal discovery, not a retry of a failed query. Worker original capped ACK wait remains.

known_issue_dispositions.issue: later worker receipt replaces earlier memory cause
known_issue_dispositions.support: Pending failure queue adopts the first retained cause. Worker receipt is imported without overwriting earlier parent cause; conflicts are retained separately. Terminal embeds latched first failure and rechecks its identity, not merely its code.

known_issue_dispositions.issue: temporary empty group map during observation
known_issue_dispositions.support: No clear-then-update window: retained groups are removed individually only when dispositioned, while surviving keys remain present for unlocked signalling snapshots.
Production parser rejects empty rows, runner omission, empty birth and duplicate PIDs; failed observation cannot become empty closure.
ps Popen is registered before waiting; helper reap and birth/exit are recorded and live helper remains in children if unreaped. Late-spawn stop handling remains open.

completed_checks.result: Read complete current source, baseline-to-candidate changes and adopted proposal. Parent includes original absolute_deadline_utc in context before hashing it; worker uses UTC soft remainder rather than sharing parent monotonic origin. Context hash/nonce/environment/actual parent/group/birth are validated before ACK.

Ordinary cap2.0 and cleanup cap0.5 remain capped by original soft/hard deadlines. Query intent precedes recomputation immediately at launch. Failed queries latch before completion logging; production adapter uses one Popen/communicate, no query retry, and launch/parse/OS errors fail closed. All production queries now serialize through audit_lock, avoiding shared query_launch cross-talk. No empirical sufficiency claim.

Direct children and ps helpers are memory-registered before waiting; validated group binds before ACK I/O. Registry snapshot persistence is serialized. Discovered identity and exit/reuse history retained; unknown handles remain OBS03. Unseen detached/reparented descendants remain outside complete historical coverage.

Worker visible stop codes limited1..255 with malformed/overflow default1. Query error budget/elapsed/class recorded as structured first failure. Parent publishes first failure and stop marker from main; worker checkpoint sees only published files. Phase crossing before visibility remains explicitly possible. Group cleanup is still responsible.

Soft timer/signalling independent of global query and receipt/audit waits in intended path. Hard_stop uses direct signals, per-target exception isolation and unconditional finally exit124. Main alone writes normal audit/terminal; observer only requests stop. OBS01 blocks prompt early observer stop during Popen and OBS02 permits late registration after escalation.

completed_checks.scope: Final failure serialization and audit freshness
completed_checks.result: Production main quiesces observer, performs fresh cleanup-budget audit after input postflight, then prepares terminal outside latch and atomically rechecks code plus first-failure identity under state/failure locks. decision refuses pending stops, missing ACK, non-CLEAR/nonempty audit or soft-deadline exhaustion. The production call sequence supplies freshness; decision itself trusts caller-supplied audit/quiet values and has no query-ID freshness assertion. This is not an independently qualified control or arbitrary-input security guarantee.
